content.text: I need to examine the OIDC authentication service, auth configuration, and environment setup files to understand the current implementation and design a concrete solution for this question.

For Okta integration with OIDC, I need to configure a groups claim on the Okta side—either through the org authorization server or a custom one—and request the `groups` scope to retrieve group information in the ID or access token.

On the nao side, better-auth's `genericOAuth` plugin supports `getUserInfo`, `mapProfileToUser`, and `overrideUserInfo`, so I can capture and map those groups to roles. The tricky part is that role mapping needs to happen on every sign-in, not just at user creation. The session creation hook runs on every authentication, which is ideal, but it doesn't have direct access to the OIDC profile data. I could decode the stored `idToken` from the account table during the session hook to extract the groups, or explore other approaches to sync the groups on each login. content.text: I need to verify whether `mapProfileToUser` gets called on every sign-in or just during account creation, and whether the userInfo includes the raw profile data with groups information — that'll determine if roles can be synced from the OAuth provider.

input.description: Find mapProfileToUser usage in better-auth dist

content.text: I need to verify whether the default `getUserInfo` function from the oauth2 utilities returns the complete profile object including the `groups` field, since that's what gets passed to `mapProfileToUser` for transformation.

input.command: grep -rn "async function getUserInfo\|function getUserInfo" node_modules/better-auth/dist/shared/*.mjs node_modules/better-auth/dist/*.mjs 2>/dev/null | head -20

content.text:
The `getUserInfo` function spreads all the decoded ID token claims into `userInfo`, so if Okta includes `groups` in the token, it'll be available there. When `mapProfileToUser` receives this full set of claims, it only returns a partial user object that gets merged in — but since role isn't stored on the user table itself, and this mapping runs on every sign-in, there's a question about how to handle the role data.

The recommended approach is to store the groups as an additional field on the user record (like `ssoGroups` as a JSON or comma-separated text column), extract them in `mapProfileToUser`, and then use `overrideUserInfo: true` to refresh the groups on each login. The trade-off is that `overrideUserInfo` will also refresh name, email, and image on every sign-in — which keeps the user data in sync with the IdP but means any edits users make locally would get overwritten. I need to check whether `overrideUserInfo` actually updates additional fields or just the core user properties.

There are other options worth considering: running the group reconciliation in a request hook after the OAuth callback, using a custom `getUserInfo` function in the OIDC config to call the Okta Groups API directly, or hooking into the session creation flow to extract and map groups on every login.

The cleanest approach might be a hybrid — let `mapProfileToUser` handle storing groups in a `ssoGroups` column during user creation, then use either `overrideUserInfo` or a session hook to refresh that data on each sign-in. I need to verify whether the sign-in flow updates the account's idToken and check how `overrideUserInfoOnSignIn` works.

content.text:
I'm realizing that when `overrideUserInfo` is true, it would attempt to write all the merged claims directly as user fields through an update call, which could cause issues since better-auth's adapter typically only recognizes specific schema fields and might reject or silently ignore unknown ones.

Actually, the adapter does filter through schema transformation, so unknown fields get dropped but declared additional fields like `ssoGroups` would persist. The concern is that with all raw claims merged in, standard fields like name and email get overwritten from the IdP on every login—which is expected behavior for IdP-managed SSO but worth noting.

There's also another path: since the account's `idToken` gets refreshed on every sign-in through the `updateAccountOnSignIn` flow, I could use a `session.create.after` hook to read the fresh token from the account row. That would work without needing `overrideUserInfo`, though it's less clean and couples the session hook to the account table.

The cleanest approach would be a dedicated service function for syncing roles from SSO groups, called from both the user creation hook (where `ssoGroups` would already be populated from `mapProfileToUser`) and the session creation hook (which runs on every sign-in and can look up the user's current `ssoGroups`). With `overrideUserInfo: true`, the `ssoGroups` column gets refreshed before the session is created, so the timing works out.

Actually, I can simplify further — just handle everything in `session.create.after` since it fires right after user creation anyway, and the user creation hook already handles org bootstrapping. The session hook would read the user's `ssoGroups`, resolve the appropriate role, and upsert the membership records, potentially overriding the default role that was set during user creation. But I need to be careful here: `session.create.after` fires for every session creation, including email/password logins and refreshes, so I should only run the group-mapping logic when the user actually has an OIDC account with `ssoGroups` populated.

Now looking at the Okta side — I need to understand how to configure group claims in Okta, specifically whether to use the org authorization server or a custom one.

For the org auth server, I can set up group claims directly in the OIDC app's Sign On tab by configuring the Groups claim type with a filter expression (like matching a regex pattern), which puts the groups directly in the ID token without needing a separate scope.

Alternatively, with a custom authorization server through API Access Management, I'd add a groups claim that includes groups in the ID token, filtered by regex, though this requires an API AM license.

There's a limit on how many groups Okta includes in the claim

—if there are more than 100, I'd need to either filter with a prefix or fetch groups from the userinfo endpoint or the Groups API instead. Since better-auth's default behavior prefers the ID token when it has the subject and email, I need to make sure the groups claim is in the ID token itself, or write a custom `getUserInfo` function that fetches from both the ID token and the userinfo endpoint to merge them together for complete coverage.

For the mapping config, I'm setting up environment variables to define the groups claim name, role mappings from group names to roles with a precedence order (admin > context_admin > user > viewer), a default role for unmapped users, and a flag to enable role syncing. At the org level, context_admin doesn't exist, so I'd map it to user for org membership while keeping context_admin at the project level.

When syncing, I need to update both the org member role (downgrading context_admin to user) and the project member role for the default project. I also need to handle users in no mapped groups—either deny login or assign the default role—and decide whether to prevent demotion of manually-set roles or treat the IdP as the source of truth. On the UI side, the role editor in the team settings should become read-only when group mapping is enabled, with a note that roles are managed by the identity provider. This is an Enterprise feature, so it needs the appropriate license header.

I'm also noting that while Azure AD's groups claim returns GUIDs rather than names, the same service pattern could work there, but the current ask is specifically for Okta. Let me check the environment configuration for OIDC settings and review the existing auth documentation to understand the patterns I should follow.
